title: one, holy, catholic
hookLine: one, holy, catholic — the small-c word means universal
tomorrow: the saint who wrote about prayer like a friendship

cards: A Catholic Mass in Lagos. In Manila. In a tiny village in Poland.
In a strip-mall parish in Texas. The language is different. The music is wildly different: drums, organs, guitars, choirs in five-part harmony.
But a regular would know where they were almost at once. The readings, the peace, the table. The same shape, in a language you don't speak.
Every Sunday, Catholics say a creed that calls the Church one, holy, catholic and apostolic. Today, the small-c word in that line, and what it actually means.

teach.b: Start with church. In the New Testament the Greek word is ekklesia, from a verb meaning to call out. It meant an assembly, people called out of their houses to gather.
So the Church, first of all, isn't a building. It's the people who were called. Now the small-c word.
Catholic comes from the Greek katholikos, from kath' holou: according to the whole. Universal.

teach.h: IGNATIUS, ON THE ROAD TO ROME.
teach.b: Early in Christian history, a bishop named Ignatius of Antioch was being taken to Rome under guard, to be executed. On the way he wrote letters to the churches.
In one of them he writes that wherever Jesus Christ is, there is the catholic Church.
He meant the whole Church, everywhere, gathered around Christ. The creed said at Sunday Mass puts four words side by side. One: many countries, one faith.
Holy: set apart for God, even though, as day five said, its people are far from perfect. Catholic: for everyone, everywhere. Apostolic: going back to the apostles.
Catholics believe their Church is one family under the pope, the bishop of Rome, successor of Peter. And that family is more varied than it looks.
Alongside the Latin Church there are Eastern Catholic Churches, with their own liturgies and traditions, united with Rome. Other Christians say these creed words too.
Orthodox Christians say catholic and mean the Orthodox Church. In Protestant churches that say the creed, it usually means the whole Church of Christ across every denomination.
For Catholics, Ignatius's line still sets the size of the word: wherever Christ is.

how: Every Sunday at Mass, Catholics profess a creed, usually the Nicene Creed, including belief in "one, holy, catholic and apostolic Church," and pray for the pope and the local bishop by name.

games.q: you're Ignatius, a bishop under guard on the road to Rome, where you'll be executed. what do you do with the time?
games.why: he wrote letters. in one of them: wherever Jesus Christ is, there is the catholic Church.

practice: Here's the practice. Picture the globe, slowly turning. Somewhere it's morning, and people are walking into a church.
Somewhere it's midnight, and someone is praying alone by a candle. Somewhere a baby is being baptized, and somewhere a funeral is ending. Let the picture be as big as it wants to be.
You're one person on it, breathing. If you pray, you can pray for all of them at once.

wordCard.voice: The Church. The ekklesia, the people called out, and catholic, meaning according to the whole: universal. Nineteenth word.

orig.note: Greek: universal, according to the whole, from kath' holou.

carryVoice: Your line: everywhere at once. Lagos, Manila, Texas, and wherever you're sitting. Day nineteen, done.
